correctness.rationale: Binomial log convolution follows from exact polar-weight iteration. Uniform binomial moment bounds and strict Gaussian small-ball monotonicity give the sharp general norm exponent. The exact binomial absolute-deviation identity, Berry–Esseen CDF error with integrated increments, Gaussian convexity and global tail bound justify the local Laplace window and the full Schatten sum, including the constant. Quadratic moments yield exact theta formulas and orbit closures. The companion Python checker independently passed 3276 finite checks; infinite conclusions rest on the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The problem is the rate and spectral multiplicity of generalized Aluthge convergence for compact weighted shifts, which qualitative norm/Schatten convergence does not measure. One natural bilaterally decaying family gives a sharp all-shape logarithmic exponent, a nontrivial n^{1/4}-width Gaussian norm-to-Schatten divergence for Laplace decay, and exact lattice-pinned arithmetic variation for quadratic decay; these are structurally different and motivated spectral windows, not arbitrary finite invariant calculations.
